name: Muzi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation. De Gruyter (covers Muzi/Muji lects, phonology; tonal Ngwi; not readable online).

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §3.3 'Southern Muji phonology in brief' (pp. 8-9): 'Regarding suprasegmental phonology, Southern Muji features five pitch contrasts.. /55/, /33/, /13/, /21/ and /52/'; sandhi and tense-voice phonation described. MLT Muzi (Gejiu, Laochang, Malutang) is listed only as an external datapoint in the abbreviations and footnotes. a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence: no hits in 536 kB of text.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Change Request 2007-120: split of [ymj] into Muji Southern [ymc], Muji Northern [ymx], Muji Qila [ymq], Moji [ymi], Muzi [ymz]. SIL International, 8 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Intelligibility/RTT rationale only (Muzi speakers scored.50 on the Southern Muji recorded text test); cites Pelkey forthcoming 2008 La Trobe dissertation as the sole published source. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Muji's mirrored merger: correlative redistribution of checked tone classes in a newly defined Burmic cluster. Mon-Khmer Studies 37: 179-195.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2 'Sample phonology sketch' (pp. 181-183) sketches Southern Muji PJZ (syllable C(V)VT, 34 initials, 5 tones 55/33/13/21/52, tone sandhi, non-contrastive phonation); Muzi enters only as tone-data points MLT (Malutang, Gejiu) and SZT (Shizitou, Jinping). No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the 17 pages.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: toward the synthesis and statement of a sub-branch. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification/ethnolinguistic overview; Muzi appears only as an ethnonym row in the Phula-varieties table (Gejiu/Mengzi/Hekou, sources PBMZ 1990, MZXZ 1995 = county annals). Nothing on stress (the only 'stress' hits are the verb 'stresses/stressed').

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page muzi1235; Wikipedia 'Muzi language', 'Muji language', 'Phula languages'
sources.note: Names Mogeha/Muji/Muzi; refs are Pelkey 2011, Lama 2012, Campbell et al. 2022 (ELCat) only. No phonology statements. Wikipedia Muji page gives only the Qila velar-lateral affricates; nothing on stress.

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL3311.Y5 P45 2011
sources.note: The only full-length linguistic description covering Muzi (MLT datapoint); its five phonology sketches (Phola, Phuza, Southern Muji, Hlepho Phowa, Azha) are the fullest Phula phonologies in print and the most likely place for any remark on stress/prominence in the Muji clade. Content on stress unverified.
